# AiroHub

> A collaborative 3D spray-paint studio that runs in a browser tab. Put a real
> 3D object on a big screen, and up to four phones become spray cans pointed at
> it. Everyone paints the same object at the same time. No install, no account,
> one six-character room code.

This file follows the llms.txt community convention (llmstxt.org). It is a
convention, not a web standard: nothing is obliged to read it, and nothing here
is authoritative over the pages themselves. It exists because AiroHub is a
client-rendered WebGL app whose interesting content lives in a JavaScript
bundle, and a plain-text pointer costs nothing.

## Pages

- https://airohub.netlify.app/ — the landing page and the entry point. Creates a
  studio (a room) or joins one with a code.
- https://airohub.netlify.app/how-it-works — the field guide. A plain-language
  walkthrough of the big screen and of the phone, which can be held two ways:
  aimed at the screen like a can, or painted on directly. Includes an object you
  can paint in the page and a list of common questions.

## How it works, in one paragraph

A phone sends where it is pointing, and nothing else. The studio puts paint on
the object exactly where the phone was aimed, and that paint goes onto the
object itself rather than a layer floating in front of it, so it survives camera
moves, object swaps and a page reload. Every screen in the room draws the same
picture from the same instructions, so nobody is watching a video of somebody
else's screen.

## Not for indexing

/canvas/*, /controller/* and /admin* are live session surfaces behind throwaway
codes. They hold no durable content, they are disallowed in robots.txt, and they
are served with X-Robots-Tag: noindex.

## Requirements

A modern browser with WebGL. Free, no account, no install.
